items.front: Harsha's dynasty and original seat?
items.back: Pushyabhuti (Vardhana) dynasty; original seat Thanesar (Sthanvishvara, Haryana); capital later Kannauj.
items.source: APPSC GK — Harshavardhana

items.front: Harsha's accession year and its calendrical significance?
items.back: c. 606 CE, at age 16 — taken as the start of the Harsha era (Harshabda). Born 590 CE.
items.examPoint: Birth 590 CE, accession c.606 CE at age 16, Harsha era
items.source: APPSC GK — Harshavardhana

items.front: Who killed Harsha's brother; who was his key ally?
items.back: Shashanka of Gauda (Bengal) killed Rajyavardhan; Harsha allied with Bhaskaravarman of Kamarupa (Assam). Sister = Rajyashri.
items.examPoint: First campaign vs Shashanka of Gauda; Rajyashri & Bhaskaravarman alliance
items.source: APPSC GK — Harshavardhana

items.front: Harsha's capital and extent of his empire?
items.back: Capital Kannauj (united with Thanesar); held Punjab & central India; annexed Bengal, Bihar, Odisha; beat Vallabhi (Gujarat).
items.source: APPSC GK — Harshavardhana

items.front: Who defeated Harsha, when, and what became the boundary?
items.back: Chalukya Pulakeshin II (of Vatapi) defeated him in 618–619 CE; the Narmada became the southern boundary.
items.examPoint: Defeat by Pulakeshin II (618-619 CE) & Narmada boundary
items.source: APPSC GK — Harshavardhana

items.front: Harsha's religious trajectory?
items.back: Shaiva (Hindu) Brahmin until c.631 CE, then embraced Mahayana Buddhism (via Rajyashri & Hiuen-Tsang); stayed secular/tolerant.
items.examPoint: Religion — Shaiva Brahmin to Mahayana Buddhism; secular
items.source: APPSC GK — Harshavardhana

items.front: Harsha's own three Sanskrit plays?
items.back: Ratnavali (4 acts, early Holi reference), Priyadarshika, and Nagananda (Buddhist theme).
items.examPoint: Harsha as author — three Sanskrit plays (Ratnavali, Priyadarshika, Nagananda)
items.source: APPSC GK — Harshavardhana

items.front: Harsha's court poet and his works?
items.back: Banabhatta — Harshacharita (prose biography, 'Deeds of Harsha') and Kadambari (one of the world's earliest novels).
items.source: APPSC GK — Harshavardhana

items.front: Which Chinese pilgrim visited Harsha, when, and his account?
items.back: Hiuen-Tsang (Xuanzang), c. 630–643 CE (~13 yrs), 'prince of pilgrims'; account = Si-Yu-Ki.
items.source: APPSC GK — Harshavardhana

items.front: Was I-Tsing a contemporary of Harsha?
items.back: No — I-Tsing visited later (671–695 CE); he wrote biographies of Nalanda monks and focused on Vinaya rules. (Classic trap.)
items.examPoint: I-Tsing (671-695 CE) — not contemporary; Nalanda monk biographies
items.source: APPSC GK — Harshavardhana

items.front: Harsha's two great religious assemblies?
items.back: Kannauj assembly (c.643 CE, honouring Hiuen-Tsang/Mahayana) and the quinquennial Prayag (Allahabad) charity convocation.
items.source: APPSC GK — Harshavardhana

items.front: Harsha's three main taxes?
items.back: Bhaga (land tax, ~1/6 of produce), Hiranya (cash tax), Bali (additional levy).
items.examPoint: Economy — Bhaga, Hiranya & Bali taxes; revenue division
items.source: APPSC GK — Harshavardhana

items.front: Harsha's provincial hierarchy and council?
items.back: Bhukti (province, Governor) → Vishaya (district, Vishayapati) → Grama (village, Gramika); advised by a Mantri Parishad.
items.source: APPSC GK — Harshavardhana

items.front: Which university did Harsha patronise; scholarly language?
items.back: Nalanda (leading university per Hiuen-Tsang); education monastery-based; Sanskrit the language of the learned.
items.examPoint: Nalanda, education system & shifting urban centres
items.source: APPSC GK — Harshavardhana

items.front: When did Harsha die and why did the empire fall?
items.back: Died 647 CE with no heir → empire disintegrated into regional kingdoms. He was the last great ruler of northern India pre-Islamic invasions.
items.source: APPSC GK — Harshavardhana

items.front: What did Shashanka of Gauda reputedly do at Bodh Gaya?
items.back: He is said to have cut down the Bodhi tree; Shashanka was a devout Shaiva.
items.examPoint: First campaign vs Shashanka of Gauda; Rajyashri & Bhaskaravarman alliance
items.source: local APPSC GK PDF — Ancient History: The Reign of Harshavardhana; R. S. Sharma, India's Ancient Past (ch. on Harsha); NCERT Class VI/VII; Britannica — Harsha

items.front: Fate of Harsha's empire after 647 CE — who usurped?
items.back: His minister Arunashva usurped power and attacked the Chinese envoy Wang Xuance, who defeated him.
items.source: local APPSC GK PDF — Ancient History: The Reign of Harshavardhana; R. S. Sharma, India's Ancient Past (ch. on Harsha); NCERT Class VI/VII; Britannica — Harsha

items.front: What share of Harsha's taxes went to charity and culture?
items.back: About 25% — one of the four parts of revenue.
items.examPoint: Economy — Bhaga, Hiranya & Bali taxes; revenue division
items.source: local APPSC GK PDF — Ancient History: The Reign of Harshavardhana; R. S. Sharma, India's Ancient Past (ch. on Harsha); NCERT Class VI/VII; Britannica — Harsha

items.front: Role of Harsha's Mantri Parishad beyond advice?
items.back: It had a role in the selection of the king and in foreign policy; the prime minister was its top post.
items.source: local APPSC GK PDF — Ancient History: The Reign of Harshavardhana; R. S. Sharma, India's Ancient Past (ch. on Harsha); NCERT Class VI/VII; Britannica — Harsha

items.front: Common punishments under Harsha?
items.back: Banishment and cutting off limbs (maiming); trial by ordeal; life imprisonment for plotting.
items.source: local APPSC GK PDF — Ancient History: The Reign of Harshavardhana; R. S. Sharma, India's Ancient Past (ch. on Harsha); NCERT Class VI/VII; Britannica — Harsha

items.front: Is the Harshacharita in prose or verse?
items.back: Ornate Sanskrit prose (standard references); the source PDF calls it verse.
items.source: local APPSC GK PDF — Ancient History: The Reign of Harshavardhana; R. S. Sharma, India's Ancient Past (ch. on Harsha); NCERT Class VI/VII; Britannica — Harsha

items.front: Banabhatta's period?
items.back: Banabhatta is dated 606–647 CE — Harsha's reign.
items.source: local APPSC GK PDF — Ancient History: The Reign of Harshavardhana; R. S. Sharma, India's Ancient Past (ch. on Harsha); NCERT Class VI/VII; Britannica — Harsha

items.front: What did Hiuen-Tsang take back to China?
items.back: Sacred Buddhist texts and relics.
items.source: local APPSC GK PDF — Ancient History: The Reign of Harshavardhana; R. S. Sharma, India's Ancient Past (ch. on Harsha); NCERT Class VI/VII; Britannica — Harsha

items.front: Hiuen-Tsang's four divisions of society?
items.back: Brahmins, Kshatriyas, Vaishyas and Shudras — caste rigid but without social conflict.
items.source: local APPSC GK PDF — Ancient History: The Reign of Harshavardhana; R. S. Sharma, India's Ancient Past (ch. on Harsha); NCERT Class VI/VII; Britannica — Harsha

items.front: Hiuen-Tsang on lifestyles of different classes?
items.back: Brahmanas and Kshatriyas simple; nobles and priests luxurious.
items.source: local APPSC GK PDF — Ancient History: The Reign of Harshavardhana; R. S. Sharma, India's Ancient Past (ch. on Harsha); NCERT Class VI/VII; Britannica — Harsha

items.front: Hiuen-Tsang's view of Indian character?
items.back: Short-tempered but hygienic and honest.
items.source: local APPSC GK PDF — Ancient History: The Reign of Harshavardhana; R. S. Sharma, India's Ancient Past (ch. on Harsha); NCERT Class VI/VII; Britannica — Harsha

items.front: Hiuen-Tsang on meat-eating?
items.back: People were encouraged to give up meat; fish and mutton occasionally; beef forbidden.
items.source: local APPSC GK PDF — Ancient History: The Reign of Harshavardhana; R. S. Sharma, India's Ancient Past (ch. on Harsha); NCERT Class VI/VII; Britannica — Harsha

items.front: Common foods under Harsha?
items.back: Sugar, milk, ghee and rice.
items.source: local APPSC GK PDF — Ancient History: The Reign of Harshavardhana; R. S. Sharma, India's Ancient Past (ch. on Harsha); NCERT Class VI/VII; Britannica — Harsha

items.front: Dress and crafts in Harsha's time?
items.back: Colourful cotton and silk; weaving of fine cloth reached perfection; women used cosmetics.
items.source: local APPSC GK PDF — Ancient History: The Reign of Harshavardhana; R. S. Sharma, India's Ancient Past (ch. on Harsha); NCERT Class VI/VII; Britannica — Harsha

items.front: Who were respected for wisdom in Harsha's time?
items.back: Wandering bhikkhus and sadhus.
items.examPoint: Nalanda, education system & shifting urban centres
items.source: local APPSC GK PDF — Ancient History: The Reign of Harshavardhana; R. S. Sharma, India's Ancient Past (ch. on Harsha); NCERT Class VI/VII; Britannica — Harsha

items.front: Feudalism in Harsha's time — definition and status?
items.back: Nobles held land in exchange for military service; land rights were socially superior.
items.source: local APPSC GK PDF — Ancient History: The Reign of Harshavardhana; R. S. Sharma, India's Ancient Past (ch. on Harsha); NCERT Class VI/VII; Britannica — Harsha

items.front: Why did Harsha's empire break up, apart from no heir?
items.back: Feudal lords defied orders and withheld taxes, becoming feudatory independent states.
items.source: local APPSC GK PDF — Ancient History: The Reign of Harshavardhana; R. S. Sharma, India's Ancient Past (ch. on Harsha); NCERT Class VI/VII; Britannica — Harsha

items.front: Powers of village and town councils under Harsha?
items.back: Only limited powers, under the overall control of governors.
items.source: local APPSC GK PDF — Ancient History: The Reign of Harshavardhana; R. S. Sharma, India's Ancient Past (ch. on Harsha); NCERT Class VI/VII; Britannica — Harsha

items.front: Small or large kingdom — Pushyabhutis at first?
items.back: A small kingdom in northern India, centred on Thanesar.
items.source: local APPSC GK PDF — Ancient History: The Reign of Harshavardhana; R. S. Sharma, India's Ancient Past (ch. on Harsha); NCERT Class VI/VII; Britannica — Harsha

items.front: Contemporary Kalinga and Chera?
items.back: Kalinga and the Chera kingdom were also contemporaries of Harsha.
items.source: local APPSC GK PDF — Ancient History: The Reign of Harshavardhana; R. S. Sharma, India's Ancient Past (ch. on Harsha); NCERT Class VI/VII; Britannica — Harsha

items.front: Chola capital per the source — and the caveat?
items.back: Thanjavur — but it became the Chola capital only in the 9th century (Vijayalaya).
items.source: local APPSC GK PDF — Ancient History: The Reign of Harshavardhana; R. S. Sharma, India's Ancient Past (ch. on Harsha); NCERT Class VI/VII; Britannica — Harsha

items.front: Vallabhi king allied to Harsha by marriage?
items.back: Dhruvasena II, who married Harsha's daughter.
items.source: local APPSC GK PDF — Ancient History: The Reign of Harshavardhana; R. S. Sharma, India's Ancient Past (ch. on Harsha); NCERT Class VI/VII; Britannica — Harsha

items.front: From whose period did feudalism become more visible?
items.back: From Harsha's period — the impact of feudalism became more visible.
items.source: local APPSC GK PDF — Ancient History: The Reign of Harshavardhana; R. S. Sharma, India's Ancient Past (ch. on Harsha); NCERT Class VI/VII; Britannica — Harsha

items.front: When was Harsha a Shaiva?
items.back: A follower of Shiva till about 631 CE, then Mahayana Buddhism.
items.examPoint: Religion — Shaiva Brahmin to Mahayana Buddhism; secular
items.source: local APPSC GK PDF — Ancient History: The Reign of Harshavardhana; R. S. Sharma, India's Ancient Past (ch. on Harsha); NCERT Class VI/VII; Britannica — Harsha
